topicName: ArgoCD and FluxCD: Kubernetes Continuous Delivery Operators
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"ArgoCD and FluxCD: Kubernetes Continuous Delivery Operators"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to GitOps in Kubernetes"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"GitOps is an operational framework that takes DevOps best practices used for application development such as version control, collaboration, CI/CD, and applies them to infrastructure automation. In the Kubernetes ecosystem, GitOps is typically implemented using Continuous Delivery (CD) operators that run inside the cluster and reconcile the actual state with the desired state stored in a Git repository."},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Two of the most prominent tools in this space are ArgoCD and FluxCD. Both follow the GitOps methodology but differ in architecture, user experience, and extensibility. This tutorial explores their core concepts, installation, and usage."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Differences: ArgoCD vs FluxCD"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ArgoCD: Features a rich web UI, supports Helm, Kustomize, and plain YAML natively, and uses a declarative approach via Application custom resources."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"FluxCD: Highly modular, built on the GitOps Toolkit controllers, relies heavily on CRDs, and traditionally leans toward a CLI and Git-centric workflow without a mandatory heavy UI."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Installing ArgoCD"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"To install ArgoCD on your Kubernetes cluster, you create a dedicated namespace and apply the official installation manifests."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"kubectl create namespace argocd
kubectl apply -n argocd -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/argoproj/argo-cd/stable/manifests/install.yaml"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the pods are running, you can access the ArgoCD user interface by port-forwarding the API server service."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"kubectl port-forward svc/argocd-server -n argocd 8080:443"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Deploying an Application with ArgoCD"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"ArgoCD uses an Application Custom Resource Definition (CRD) to define the link between your Git repository and your target Kubernetes cluster."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: guestbook
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  project: default
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/argoproj/argocd-example-apps.git
    targetRevision: HEAD
    path: guestbook
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: default
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      prune: true
      selfHeal: true"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Installing FluxCD"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"FluxCD is bootstrapped using the Flux CLI, which configures your cluster and pushes the necessary manifests back to your Git repository."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"flux check --pre
flux bootstrap github \
  --owner=<YOUR-GITHUB-USER> \
  --repository=<YOUR-REPO-NAME> \
  --branch=main \
  --path=clusters/my-cluster \
  --personal"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Deploying an Application with FluxCD"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"FluxCD uses specialized CRDs like GitRepository and Kustomization to manage workloads. Below is an example of defining a GitRepository source."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: source.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: GitRepository
metadata:
  name: podinfo
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 1m
  url: https://github.com/stefanprodan/podinfo
  ref:
    branch: master"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Next, define the Kustomization resource to instruct Flux how to deploy the manifests from the repository."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: Kustomization
metadata:
  name: podinfo
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 5m
  sourceRef:
    kind: GitRepository
    name: podinfo
  path: ./kustomize
  targetNamespace: default
  prune: true"},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"Both ArgoCD and FluxCD provide robust, production-ready continuous delivery mechanisms for Kubernetes. ArgoCD stands out for teams requiring a comprehensive dashboard and visual synchronization status, whereas FluxCD shines for platform engineers building modular, API-driven GitOps pipelines with minimal footprint."}]
